sample.justification: Brisk, witty dialogue immediately establishes the central marriage goal and the arrival of a wealthy newcomer, creating steady forward pull.
After a brief discussion of impressions with Jane, the chapter slows into extended, static exposition detailing the Bingleys' background and Darcy's character.
Parlor conversations advance the social dynamics and character oppositions steadily, ending with the minor urgency of Jane's worsening illness.

sample.summary: For the narrative to maintain its brisk timing and escalating pressure, key socio-economic and historical conditions—such as the legal entail of Longbourn in Scene 7 (7 Jane Falls Ill.md), the long-standing Darcy-Wickham backstory revealed in Scene 35 (35 Darcy's Letter.md), and the failed failure-to-produce-a-son economy in Scene 50 (50 Mr Bennet's Regrets.md)—must already be fixed in place before the opening chapter. These pre-existing pressures compress the characters' choices, allowing scenes like Scene 1 (1 Bingley Arrives.md), Scene 13 (13 Collins Arrives.md), and Scene 46 (46 Jane's Letters.md) to generate immediate momentum without slowing for heavy exposition.

firstFinding.headline: Pre-existing marital mismatch and patriarchal visiting rules immediately drive the opening scene's momentum.
bullets: Twenty-three years of marriage have already fixed Mr. Bennet's sarcastic reserve and Mrs. Bennet's single-minded focus on marrying off her five daughters.

Regency social etiquette—requiring the father of the family to call on a male newcomer before the women can be introduced—must already hold true as an unbreakable social contract to create the opening conflict.
firstFinding.subject: Social etiquette and family dynamics

supportingRefs.quote: Mr. Bennet was so odd a mixture of quick parts, sarcastic humour, reserve, and caprice, that the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character.

firstFinding.evidenceQuote: Indeed you must go, for it will be impossible for _us_ to visit him, if you do not.
